question: Ramesh has invested Rs. 1,232 at 6% p.a. simple interest in a bank. What amount will he get after 3 years?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
Total **Simple Interest** percentage for 3 years = 6% × 3 = 18%.

Total **Amount** percentage = 100% + 18% = 118%.

Final Amount = 118% of ₹1,232 = 1.18 × 1,232.

Calculation: 1,232 × 1 + 1,232 × 0.18 = 1,232 + 221.76 = ₹1,453.76.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,453.76.**

**__Alternate Method__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/17320b369e7757dc5d65511342f184e337550d934d64c68682b58d03cf9226da.png] 
**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹1,232

Rate of Interest (R) = 6% per annum

Time (T) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = (1,232 × 6 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (1,232 × 18) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 22,176 ÷ 100 = ₹221.76

⇒ Amount (A) = 1,232 + 221.76

⇒ Amount (A) = ₹1,453.76

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,453.76.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Definition

Simple interest is calculated only on the **Principal amount** of a loan or investment, ensuring the interest remains constant every year.

Compound Interest Comparison

Unlike SI, **Compound Interest** is calculated on the principal plus the accumulated interest of previous periods: A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ.

Rule of 72

To find the approximate time needed to double your money at a given interest rate, divide 72 by the annual **Interest Rate**.
